report.source_text: Diagnostic paracentesis was performed with the resulting fluid biochemistry as follows: lactate dehydrogenase of 1255 U/L, total protein of 53 g/L, pH 7.76 and alkaline phosphatase of 51 U/L. Fluid cytology showed neoplastic cells with moderate amount of eosinophilic cytoplasm and rare papillary-like structures. Immunochemistry staining showed PAX8-positive, CD10-positive and CK7-positive cells consistent with carcinoma of renal origin (figure 3). There was no bacterial growth from the ascitic fluid culture.

report.source_text: He was subsequently reviewed by the Medical Oncology team, which commenced on 20 mg daily dose of cabozantinib, a small-molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor. He initially reported good improvement in his abdominal pain symptoms within 1 month of therapy commencement. clinician.final_diagnosis: pT2 Nx type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma (pRCC)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old man presented with worsening generalized abdominal pain, abdominal distension, and loss of appetite 5 months after undergoing a laparoscopic left radical nephrectomy. Histopathology of the nephrectomy specimen confirmed pT2 Nx type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma, nuclear grade 2, 80 mm, with negative surgical margins (E003). Current presentation workup included a CT scan, which revealed moderate-volume ascites with peritoneal nodules, right pleural effusion, and a 14 mm right apical subpleural nodule (E004). Diagnostic paracentesis showed neoplastic cells in the ascitic fluid, which were PAX8-positive, CD10-positive, and CK7-positive, consistent with carcinoma of renal origin (E005). The patient was started on cabozantinib, leading to initial improvement in abdominal pain, resolution of ascites and pleural effusion, and stable peritoneal and pulmonary nodules (E006). However, following a trial of higher dosage, the patient developed multiple symptoms, prompting dose reduction, and subsequently experienced recurrence of malignant ascites 5 months after initial presentation, requiring regular paracentesis (E007).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: The patient's primary tumor was diagnosed as pT2 Nx type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma, nuclear grade 2, with a greatest dimension of 80 mm, negative surgical margins, and no lymphovascular invasion.
The patient developed metastatic disease, evidenced by moderate-volume ascites with peritoneal nodules, right pleural effusion, and a 14 mm right apical subpleural nodule.
Ascitic fluid cytology confirmed the presence of neoplastic cells consistent with carcinoma of renal origin (PAX8-positive, CD10-positive, CK7-positive), indicating metastatic recurrence of the pRCC.
